title: The C2S Connection Handshake State Machine (RFC 6120)
solutionExplanation:
The FSM implements the RFC 6120 handshake flow:
1. wait_for_stream: Verifies domain matching in {stream_open, Domain} and advertises SASL PLAIN mechanism.
2. wait_for_sasl: Rejects any stanzas (like chat messages or IQs) with {error, not_authorized, State}. On valid SASL PLAIN Base64 token, decodes the null-delimited credentials and advances to authenticated.
3. authenticated: Receives bind_resource, constructs Full JID User@Domain/Resource, emits the IQ result, and transitions to session_established.
4. session_established: Enables full stanza routing.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does the C2S connection state machine set inet:setopts(Socket, [{active, once}]) after receiving each TCP packet instead of using {active, true}?

options.label: To implement backpressure flow control at the OS kernel socket buffer level, preventing malicious clients from flooding the BEAM process mailbox.
options.explanation: {active, once} stops the kernel from pushing packets to the process mailbox until the current packet has been fully handled.

options.label: Because {active, true} is not supported on Windows.
options.explanation: {active, true} works on all OS platforms, but lacks flow control.

options.label: Because {active, once} runs twice as fast as passive recv.
options.explanation: The primary benefit of {active, once} is mailbox protection and event-driven backpressure.

options.label: Because raw TCP sockets can only receive one packet per lifetime.
options.explanation: Sockets receive endless packets; {active, once} requests them one at a time.
